short: LipNet decoder on rtMRI (M06) and new sentence-text output (M08) are standard; one unseen-speaker split without repeats; a shared 460-sentence list likely puts training sentences in the test.
position: The paper moves the LipNet decoder onto USC-TIMIT real-time MRI (M06) and makes sentence text the output of a vocal-tract MRI decoder (M08). The decoder is standard, the field's most common articulator-video design. The text output is new among 88 vocal-tract MRI studies and goes past HMM sequence recognition of continuous rtMRI speech (Katsamanis et al., 2011), but it stays standard because one split without repeats does not meet the ahead rule. The evaluation (M12) is standard: an unseen-speaker test, stronger than the one-speaker prior, but no repeats. The strongest confound is the closed sentence list: every USC-TIMIT speaker reads the same 460 sentences, so the 40.6% PER most likely measures speaker transfer, not open sentence recognition (inference). The title overreaches: the speech is audible, and no emotion is recognized.
